title: End-of-life communications & migration checklist for legacy model versions
creator: Samir Gupta
description:
Goal: Define and operationalize a repeatable deprecation workflow for older model versions (hosted + dedicated + private) that minimizes customer disruption, provides clear migration paths, and ensures accurate performance profiles are preserved for pinned deployments. This ticket consolidates required notices, migration guides, console/UI changes, API headers/events, SDK compatibility guidance, and programmatic tooling (pin checks, auto-suggest replacements).

Background: We recently onboarded multiple model variants and identified three recurring pain points during sunsets: (1) customers unaware of upcoming EOL due to limited visibility, (2) pinned versioning breaking without automated suggestions, and (3) lack of standardized migration guidance for quantized/accelerated variants. Existing artifacts: internal PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Model+Onboarding, perf matrices: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/perf_profiles_2026_Q1.xlsx, and runtime change PR #4123 in GitHub.

Proposed workflow (high level):
1) Publish an initial "deprecation notice" in the Console and via email 90 days before EOL. Include clear timeline, recommended replacement model(s), expected perf/cost delta, and migration links.
2) Create a migration guide per replacement model: API examples, SDK code snippets, delta in token accounting, known behavioral differences, and live evaluation harness (link).
3) Add API-level deprecation header (X-Redwood-Deprecation: model="v1.23", replacement="v2.0", eol="2026-06-15") and a webhook event customers can subscribe to for changes.
4) Console UX: banner on affected model pages, per-account notice center item, and a one-click "View migration checklist" with pre-filled sample prompts and test harness.
5) Pinning safety: when a customer pins a soon-to-be-deprecated model, surface a modal with risk details and an option to auto-pin the recommended replacement + create a migration task in Console.
6) Publish a performance profile comparison card on the model page (latency P50/P95, cost per token under typical batching), and include guidance for quantized builds.
7) Sunset enforcement: after EOL a soft-fail period (14 days) where requests receive a deprecation error code but are routed to a compatible fallback; after that, hard disable for hosted tier while providing tooling for Dedicated/Private customers to re-run migrations.

Stakeholders: PM (Elena, Samir), Runtime Eng (Anika Reddy, Mateo Cruz), Console UX (Priya Shah), Docs (Liam O'Connor), SDKs (Wei Zhang), Support (Nora Blake), Legal/Privacy (for notice wording).

Deliverables:
- Standard deprecation notice template (Console + email + webhook payload)
- Migration guide template and one fully authored guide for model family "redwood-gpt-small" -> "redwood-gpt-v2-small"
- API header and webhook spec (RFC) merged to runtime repo (PR #4250)
- Console banner & migration checklist UI (designs in Figma: https://figma.com/redwood/dep-notice-9354)
- Pinning modal & auto-suggest flow implemented with metrics capturing opt-in rates
- Perf comparison card component and automated perf-profile publishing job

Acceptance criteria:
- Templates and migration guide published to Docs, with reviewer sign-offs from Runtime Eng and Support.
- Console surfaces deprecation notice for a staged internal test model and supports the one-click checklist flow.
- API header and webhook delivered and documented; internal customers can subscribe to webhook events.
- Automated perf comparison appears on the model page for new onboards.
- Onboarding playbook updated to include deprecation steps for future model families.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Customers relying on pinned behavior may experience regressions. Mitigation: extended soft-fail period + auto-suggest + targeted outreach to high-usage customers.
- Risk: Inaccurate perf profiles may mislead migration choices. Mitigation: require two independent benchmark runs and a quality check step before publish.
- Risk: Legal/regulatory constraints for Private deployments. Mitigation: include a non-disruptive migration path and a manual sign-off flow for air-gapped customers.

Timeline (proposal):
- Week 1 (Mar 2–8): Spec drafts, stakeholder alignment, RFC for API headers/webhooks.
- Week 2–3 (Mar 9–22): Console designs, docs template, runtime header implementation (internal test).
- Week 4 (Mar 23–29): Migration guide authored, perf comparison plumbing, internal beta with 3 pilot customers.
- Target launch (soft): Apr 15, 2026.

Related artifacts & links:
- PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Model+Deprecation+Playbook
- Runtime PR (internal): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4250
- Console mockups: https://figma.com/redwood/dep-notice-9354
- Migration guide draft: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/model-migration-redwood-gpt-small->v2.md

Notes and trade-offs: We intentionally favor a longer notice window (90 days) and an intermediate soft-fail window (14 days) to reduce customer support load and give Dedicated/private customers time to plan. This extends operational burden but reduces risk of breaking SLAs. The performance card will show typical workload numbers (batching 8/seq128) and call out how to re-run benchmarks for custom workloads.
